question: Should OpenClaw V1 adopt the public `api.registerReadinessCriterion` Plugin SDK contract and the four built-in hosting profiles, or should the readiness work remain core-only until that external API direction is approved?
rationale: The proposal introduces persistent Plugin SDK, config, environment, CLI, Gateway protocol, and deployment-readiness contracts. Whether those public contracts should exist is a product and compatibility decision, not a mechanical repair decision.

options.title: Approve the V1 contract
options.body: Approve the public readiness callback and built-in profiles, then require the exact-head packaged Docker matrix and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Land core-only readiness first
options.body: Remove or defer plugin registration and hosting profiles so the underlying core evaluator can be considered separately.

options.title: Decline the profile feature for now
options.body: Close or pause the stacked proposal and retain existing readiness behavior until a narrower host-contract direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve the public readiness callback and built-in profiles, then require the exact-head packaged Docker matrix and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked readiness and hosting-profile stack and can supply the design context, though final acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
